findings_qualitative.value: The molecular gas fraction of post-starburst galaxies anti-correlates with the D_n4000 spectral index and stellar population age, indicating gas declines after the last major burst of star formation.

evidence.quote: The gas fraction of post-starbursts from our sample and the literature correlates with the D𝑛4000 spectral index, a proxy of the stellar population age. This suggests that their gas content decreases after the last major burst of star formation.

findings_qualitative.value: ID83492 is undergoing an early major merger phase with two gas-rich, starbursting companions, supporting quenching mechanisms that suppress star formation without completely removing the molecular gas.

evidence.quote: Finally, one of our targets is undergoing a major merger phase with two highly star-forming companions. This hints at a picture where a perturber event (e.g., major merger) quenches star formation without completely removing the molecular gas.

claims.hypothesis: Post-starburst galaxies at z > 1 with M_* ~ 5 x 10^10 M_sun have completely exhausted or expelled their molecular gas reservoirs during quenching.
claims.experiment: Observed CO(3-2) emission with ALMA Band 4 in two z > 1 post-starburst galaxies (ID83492 and ID97148) and derived their molecular gas masses and fractions.
claims.result: Detected CO(3-2) at 5sigma and 4sigma, yielding M_H2 = (9.9 ± 1.9) x 10^9 M_sun and (4.1 ± 1.1) x 10^9 M_sun, corresponding to molecular gas fractions f_H2 ~ 8% - 16%.
claims.finding: Refuted for this mass regime; z > 1 post-starburst galaxies with M_* < 10^11 M_sun retain significant molecular gas reservoirs, disfavouring complete gas consumption and expulsion.

evidence.quote: We measure their molecular gas fraction to be 𝑓H2 = MH2/M★ ∼ 8% - 16%, consistent with 𝑧< 1 post-starburst galaxies from the literature.

Our post-SB galaxies span the lowest stellar mass range probed by currently available samples (Figure 7) and seem to have retained a significant fraction of molecular gas (𝑓H2 ∼ 8% - 16%) detected in CO(3-2),
This disfavours scenarios where the gas is consumed and expelled during strong bursts of star formation,

claims.hypothesis: Quenching in z > 1 post-starburst galaxies is driven by a suppression of star formation efficiency rather than prior removal of molecular gas.
claims.experiment: Compared the derived M_H2, L'_CO, SFR, and sSFR of the targets and literature samples in the Kennicutt-Schmidt plane and the f_H2-sSFR plane.
claims.result: Targets have SFE <= 0.1 Gyr^-1 (~10x lower than main-sequence star-forming galaxies at similar z) and lie above the f_H2-sSFR relation of star-forming galaxies.
claims.finding: Supported; gas depletion is not the direct cause of star formation suppression, and quenching mechanisms must halt star formation while leaving substantial molecular gas.

evidence.quote: The star formation efficiency of our targets is ∼ 10× lower than that of star-forming galaxies at similar redshift, and they are outliers of the 𝑓H2 - specific star formation rate (sSFR) relation of star-forming galaxies,

Also the fact that post-SBs, especially at low mass and high redshift, have higher gas fraction than expected given their sSFR favours the idea that gas is not expelled before the star formation is quenched

claims.hypothesis: The molecular gas content of post-starburst galaxies decreases with time after the last major burst of star formation.
claims.experiment: Measured D_n4000, H_delta_F, and H_gamma_F indices from VIMOS optical spectra, derived Bayesian light-weighted stellar ages, and compared f_H2 against D_n4000 and age across z > 0.5 and z < 0.5 samples.
claims.result: Galaxies with higher f_H2 preferentially have lower D_n4000 (1.166 for ID97148 vs 1.407 for ID83492) and younger stellar ages (log(age/yr) = 8.6 vs 8.9).
claims.finding: Supported; molecular gas fraction decreases with increasing D_n4000 and stellar population age after the starburst episode.

evidence.quote: When considering galaxies detected in CO at 𝑧> 0.5 − 1.5 (our sample and Spilker et al. 2018; Bezanson et al. 2022; Belli et al. 2021) we find that galaxies with higher gas fraction preferentially have lower D𝑛4000 (Figure 8, top panels)

the gas fraction of post-SBs seems to decrease with the age of their stellar population (Figure 8), as suggested also by previous literature works studying lower-redshift post-SBs (French et al. 2015; Bezanson et al. 2022).

claims.hypothesis: Major mergers play a role in quenching star formation in high-redshift post-starburst galaxies while leaving a substantial molecular gas reservoir.
claims.experiment: Searched the ALMA Band 4 cubes and HST/WFC3 imaging around the post-starburst targets for companion galaxies.
claims.result: Serendipitously detected two gas-rich, starbursting companions around ID83492 in CO(3-2) (14sigma and 16.5sigma) and continuum at velocity offsets < 250 km s^-1, projected distances 48 and 112 kpc, and stellar mass ratios 1:1 and 1:1.5.
claims.finding: Supported; ID83492 is in an early major merger phase, consistent with interactions halting star formation via turbulence or heating without completely removing the ISM.

evidence.quote: Their redshift, estimated from the CO emission, is Δ𝑧< 0.0018 (𝑣off < 250 km s−1) different from that of our postSB target. This suggests that ID83492 might be in an early (multiple) merger stage.
Given the stellar masses of the companions, this is a major merger (mass ratios 1:1 and 1:1.5).
The fact that at least one of our post-SBs is undergoing a merger suggests that interactions might be a major cause for the suppression of star formation.

why_this_data.value: Targeting CO(3-2) at z > 1 probes the dense molecular gas phase during the main quenching epoch of lower-mass (M_* ~ 5 x 10^10 M_sun) post-starburst galaxies with secure spectroscopic redshifts and stringent SFR limits.

evidence.quote: In this study we expand upon those works, including two postSB galaxies at 𝑧> 1, with lower stellar masses (M★ ∼ 5 × 1010M⊙) than other high-redshift samples from the literature, allowing us to start widening the explored parameter space.
we selected two objects with stringent star formation rate limits

why_this_method.value: Since targets are unresolved at ~1.5'' resolution, modelling point sources directly in the uv plane per channel and iterating spatial positions maximizes S/N; excluding dust-based literature gas estimates avoids systematic discrepancies.

evidence.quote: To have a sample with homogeneously-derived molecular gas masses, we only considered galaxies with CO observations. We excluded from the literature comparison the galaxies with molecular gas mass estimates based on SED fitting and/or dust continuum observations.
Since our targets are expected to be unresolved at the angular resolution of the observations

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: CO emission of ID97148 originating from a nearby dust-obscured satellite not detected in near-IR imaging rather than the post-SB itself (in which case M_H2 is an upper limit)

evidence.quote: Alternatively the CO emission might originate from a nearby dust-obscured satellite which is not detected in the near-infrared imaging (e.g., Schreiber et al. 2018). In this case the molecular gas mass that we estimate for ID97148 should be considered as an upper limit.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Continuum source near ID97148 rejected as a physical companion and considered a spurious detection or lower-redshift, low-mass interloper

evidence.quote: Given the angular distance from ID97148, the redshift difference of Δ𝑧> 0.15 and the highly uncertain values retrieved from the SED fit, we do not consider such detection as a companion galaxy, but rather as a spurious detection or lower-redshift and low-mass interloper.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Post-SB ID83492 being a quiescent galaxy replenished with molecular gas stripped from its star-forming companions during the merger

evidence.quote: Another possible scenario is the fact that the post-SB is a quiescent galaxy which was replenished with molecular gas, stripped

limitations_admitted.value: Small sample size of two post-starburst galaxies at z > 1

evidence.quote: Having in the future larger samples of high-redshift post-SBs with CO observations will allow us to confirm the results reported in this study.

limitations_admitted.value: Uncertainties do not account for systematic differences in unconstrained CO excitation (r_32) and CO-to-H2 conversion factor (alpha_CO) in post-starburst galaxies

evidence.quote: These uncertainties do not account for systematic differences in the (unconstrained) excitation and CO-to-H2 factors in post-SB galaxies, but allow to directly compare our results with the literature on star-forming and quiescent galaxies.

limitations_admitted.value: Coarse angular resolution (~1.5'') leaves targets spatially unresolved, preventing detection of close pairs (< 1.5'') or morphological asymmetries and contributing to positional offset uncertainty in ID97148

evidence.quote: Observations with better angular resolution are needed to understand whether ID97148 is undergoing a late merger phase with two nuclei which are not resolved with the current angular resolution (pair closer than ∼ 1′′.5 ∼ 12.5 kpc at 𝑧 ∼ 1.2).

limitations_admitted.value: Negative noise peak next to ID97148 in the continuum map affects the measured CO(3-2) flux and line width by a factor of 2-3 depending on whether a negative continuum is fitted

evidence.quote: We also highlight that next to the CO(3-2) detected line there is a negative noise peak which is evident in the continuum map (Figure 1) and that could hide part of the emission and artificially offset its peak.

referee_caveats_inferred: The CO(3-2) detection of ID97148 is low S/N (4 sigma), spatially offset by ~1.6'' from the H-band peak, and sits on a negative continuum trough that changes the derived gas mass by a factor of >3 depending on baseline treatment.
Assuming fixed r_32 = 0.5 and Milky Way alpha_CO = 4.4 for both post-starburst targets and starbursting companions (sSFR > 10 Gyr^-1) may introduce systematic biases in M_H2.
Note that in Table 3, log(f_H2) for '97148 corrected' is printed identically as -1.0 ± 0.1 despite M_H2 increasing from 4.1 to 13.8 x 10^9 M_sun.
